profile.headline: 🎧 Audio Tools Software Engineer at Sigma Connectivity | C++, JUCE, TypeScript, DSP Tools, Creative Software
profile.summary:
I build digital audio software and creative tools that balance responsiveness, performance, reliability, and musical feel.

I work across TypeScript/JavaScript Web UIs and JUCE-based C++ audio systems, designing tools that integrate modern interface layers with real-time, timing-critical backends. My experience spans Web UI architecture, desktop audio applications, DAW plugin development, DSP workflows, and performance-sensitive creative tools.

At Sigma Connectivity Inc., I develop internal audio tooling for complex audio workflows, including client assignment work with Meta Reality Labs / XR Sonic supporting the tuning process for Ray-Ban Meta glasses. My work focuses on web-based interfaces embedded within C++ desktop environments, modular tuning components, shared UI systems, legacy workflow modernization, and tools that help audio engineers configure, inspect, and iterate on wearable audio behavior.

Previously, I founded Advanced Soundware, where I built music technology products focused on expressive musical performance, including JUCE-based desktop/plugin software, custom GUI systems, audio pipelines, and notation-driven workflows.

Earlier in my career at NBCUniversal, I supported uptime-critical broadcast and post-production systems, building a strong foundation in reliability, operational rigor, and production-focused engineering.
Outside of engineering, I compose, record, and mix orchestral music, which keeps me grounded in how creative tools are actually used.

positions.title: Software Engineer, Audio Tools
positions.description:
Client assignment: Meta Reality Labs / XR Sonic.

Developed internal audio tooling for XR Sonic workflows supporting the tuning process for Ray-Ban Meta glasses. Worked across JavaScript Web UIs and C++/JUCE desktop application architecture, building modern interfaces for complex audio tuning, capture, playback, visualization, and DSP-control workflows.

• Developed and shipped modular GUI components for an internal desktop audio tuning application used by audio engineers to configure and inspect wearable audio behavior.
• Designed and implemented approximately 12 plugin-style tuning components, replacing legacy functionality while preserving expected audio behavior and enabling new DSP controls through a modernized user experience.
• Built web-based interfaces embedded within a C++ desktop environment using JUCE, bridging native application logic with responsive browser-based UI layers.
• Created and maintained a shared JavaScript/CSS GUI Design System with reusable components and design tokens, improving consistency, reducing code duplication, and supporting broader UI modernization across the toolchain.
• Re-implemented and modernized legacy DSP-adjacent tooling behavior from incomplete specifications and existing workflows, helping preserve regression-sensitive audio behavior while improving maintainability.
• Developed audio-oriented meters, controls, visualizations, and workflow-specific UI components for tuning and analysis tasks.
• Collaborated with client engineers, designers, and audio specialists to translate tuning workflows into usable, maintainable engineering tools.
• Contributed to a modernized internal toolchain that improved usability, visual clarity, and future feature development for wearable audio tuning workflows.

Note: Work performed under client confidentiality; proprietary source code, internal demos, screenshots, and implementation details are not publicly shareable.

projects.title: Multiband Compressor — Interactive Audio DSP & Visualization Demo
projects.description:
Designed and implemented an interactive multiband audio compressor demo that combines real-time DSP concepts with a polished, production-quality frontend.

Built using TypeScript, React, and the Web Audio API, the project simulates a three-band compressor (low / mid / high) with adjustable crossovers, per-band compression controls, bypass logic, and gain-reduction metering. The UI mirrors professional audio tools, emphasizing clarity, responsiveness, and musician-friendly interaction.

Key features include:
- Real-time waveform visualization (input vs. output) synchronized to playback
- Animated meters for input level, output level, and per-band gain reduction
- Custom rotary knob controls with precise pointer interaction and value feedback
- Playback transport and scrubber with accurate time tracking
- Clean separation of concerns between audio engine, metering, animation hooks, and UI components

Architecturally, the project emphasizes:
- Strong React + TypeScript idioms (custom hooks, refs vs state, animation loops)
- Deterministic rendering for high-frequency visual updates
- A scalable component structure suitable for more advanced DSP engines

This project serves as both a DSP visualization sandbox and a demonstration of building complex, stateful, real-time interfaces in the browser — bridging audio engineering concepts with modern frontend architecture.

projects.title: D-Quant
projects.description: D-Quant is a C++ toolkit for expressive MIDI generation, modeling performance nuance through data-driven analysis and synthesis of rhythm and dynamics. It provides command-line tools and modular libraries for analyzing performance envelopes, rhythm deviations, and generating expressive single-note MIDI events.
